newsitem.title: UK: Lira wobbly pre-EU forecasts but impact seen muted.
newsitem.headline: Lira wobbly pre-EU forecasts but impact seen muted.

text.p: The Italian lira tottered again in morning Europe as the market awaited the European Union's 1997/98 forecasts to gauge member states' readiness for EMU.
Newspaper reports have suggested the EU Commission will not predict budget deficit/GDP ratios above the 3.0 percent Maastricht target for any countries expect Italy and Greece.
But analysts said the perceived political nature of the forecasts would colour, and probably muffle, market reactions.
"This is another set of forecasts thrown into the pot and the EU is going to be viewed as biased (to convergence) anyway," said Roger Francis, senior analyst at IBJ International here.

"If they say the German deficit is 3.0 percent of GDP, the reaction will be 'ha, it's a fiddle'. On the other side, if it's at 3.2 percent, the reaction will be it's over-pessimistic. So it doesn't matter either way what the forecasts are," he said.
BankAmerica economist Jeremy Hawkins agreed. The forecasts "appear to give more information on relative political weight than the chances of meeting the convergence criteria," he said.
Leaks have suggested the Commission will forecast a 1997 deficit/GDP ratio of 3.2 percent for Italy.
The lira was trading at 997.05/25 per mark at 0810 GMT, down from late Tuesday's European level of 955.50/90.
Italy's La Repubblica newspaper said in an unsourced report today that the EU would forecast the Italian deficit at 3.1 percent of GDP in 1997.
It said the Commission had rewritten its review of EU economic and budgetary conditions after lobbying by Italian officials.

Data out yesterday from key Italian cities showed April CPI heading for a 28-year low of 1.7 percent year-on-year. Analysts said this argued more strongly than ever for an interest rate cut -- which they said should support the lira -- but the currency's weakness threatened to delay monetary easing.

In its 1996 annual report, the Bundesbank said budget deficits in most European countries remained too high. It hit out at "balance sheet cosmetics" and said sustainability would be vital for countries entering monetary union.
The Buba warned of "considerable setbacks in interest rate and exchanges rate developments" for states which had benefited from convergence trades should EMU expectations be disappointed.
Elsewhere, the French franc held steady, supported by an opinion poll -- the first since the snap May 25/June 1 election was called on Monday -- which indicated the centre-right would maintain power.
Markets have been afraid the Socialists could win the election and jeopardize the budgetary restraint necessary for France to qualify for EMU.
The franc was quoted at 3.3735/40 per mark at 0834 GMT, up from yesterday's closing European level of 3.3755/59.
